primary_action.input: From the failed “chain saw” search, press Tab three times to “Search for pruning saw”, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show one available Folding Pruning Saw and leave keyboard focus easy to locate.
primary_action.observed: The field changed to “pruning saw” and retained a visible focus ring. One Folding Pruning Saw appeared with an “Available” badge. The status read “1 match. Folding Pruning Saw is available.”

1A-1440.edge_observation: Select All and Backspace emptied the focused field. “Enter a tool name” replaced the result. The pruning-saw suggestion and “1 tool available” remained visible.
1A-1440.weakness: The small “1 tool available” beside the suggestion leaves the reader to infer which query the count describes.
1A-1440.repair: Change the count to “1 pruning saw available” beside the suggestion.
1A-1440.strength: The pegboard changes from a dashed outline of the missing chain saw to a solid drawing of the available folding saw. The illustration communicates the search outcome.

primary_action.input: Press Tab three times to the full-width “Search for pruning saw” button, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Find the available saw and keep the result and keyboard focus visible at phone width.
primary_action.observed: “Folding Pruning Saw” and its checked “Available” badge appeared above the illustration. The outlined search field held “pruning saw”. The status also named the available tool.

1A-390.edge_observation: Select All and Backspace cleared the field in place. The saw result disappeared. “Enter a tool name”, the suggestion, and “1 tool available” were visible.
1A-390.weakness: The drawing of the unavailable chain saw takes up nearly half the no-match panel on the phone.
1A-390.repair: Make the illustration shallower in the mobile no-match state and keep the larger drawing for the available tool.
1A-390.strength: The yellow suggestion spans the text column above the artwork. After activation, the tool name and availability occupy that same prominent position.

primary_action.input: From “chain saw”, press Tab three times to “Search for pruning saw”, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show one available Folding Pruning Saw with a clear focus target.
primary_action.observed: One Folding Pruning Saw appeared with “Available”. Focus visibly outlined the heading “1 match for ‘pruning saw’”. The search field contained “pruning saw” and the status region was empty.

1B-1440.edge_observation: Two Shift+Tabs returned focus to the field through Search. Select All and Backspace emptied it. The old match heading, Folding Pruning Saw, and “Available” all remained visible.
1B-1440.weakness: An empty query still presents the pruning saw as a current match.
1B-1440.repair: When the field becomes empty, remove the old result and show an empty-search prompt with focus still in the field.
1B-1440.strength: The visible outline on the match-count heading locates the new result immediately above the illustrated tool.

primary_action.input: Press Tab three times to “Search for pruning saw”, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show the available saw and make the result easy to locate on the narrow screen.
primary_action.observed: Focus moved to the visibly outlined “1 match for ‘pruning saw’” heading. Folding Pruning Saw and its “Available” badge appeared directly below it. The status region was empty.

1B-390.edge_observation: After two Shift+Tabs, Select All and Backspace cleared the focused field. The panel continued to show one match for “pruning saw” and the available tool.
1B-390.weakness: The blank field and the card still naming “pruning saw” give conflicting accounts of the search.
1B-390.repair: Replace the match card with “Enter a tool name” as soon as the last character is deleted.
1B-390.strength: The recovery button, focused result heading, and availability badge are all readable above the illustration without scrolling.

primary_action.input: Press Tab to “Reserve shift” on the Wednesday 4–6 pm Packing card, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show exactly one upcoming Packing booking and move focus to an understandable confirmation.
primary_action.observed: One Packing card appeared under “Upcoming shifts” with “Wednesday 4–6 pm” and “Shift booked”. A visible focus outline enclosed the whole booked card. The reserve button disappeared.

2A-1440.edge_observation: After one reload, exactly one Packing booking remained with the same time and confirmation. Focus returned to the document body.
2A-1440.weakness: The small “Shift booked” badge is easy to overlook beneath the large Packing title on the wide card.
2A-1440.repair: Increase the confirmation text size and place the checked label beside the day and time.
2A-1440.strength: The bold time, packing-box illustration, and card-wide focus outline make it easy to verify which shift received the booking.

primary_action.input: Press Tab to the full-width “Reserve shift” button, then Space.
primary_action.expected: Reserve Wednesday 4–6 pm Packing once and keep the confirmation and shift details visible together.
primary_action.observed: The empty schedule and reserve button gave way to one Packing card. Focus outlined the card containing Wednesday, 4–6 pm, and the checked “Shift booked” label.

2A-390.edge_observation: One reload preserved exactly one Wednesday 4–6 pm Packing booking and its “Shift booked” label. Focus returned to the document body.
2A-390.weakness: Before booking, “No upcoming shifts” sits directly above an available Wednesday shift. The empty message leaves whose schedule it describes unclear.
2A-390.repair: Change the empty row to “You haven’t booked a shift yet.”
2A-390.strength: The weekday and bold time stack beside the parcel illustration, leaving the full card width for the reserve button.

primary_action.input: Press Tab to “Reserve shift” on the Wednesday 4–6 pm Packing card, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Show one booked shift with a visible, focused confirmation.
primary_action.observed: One Packing card showed Wednesday 4–6 pm. Focus moved directly to the outlined “Shift booked” paragraph beneath the time. The reserve button disappeared.

2B-1440.edge_observation: After one reload, the single booking, time, and “Shift booked” confirmation remained. Focus returned to the document body.
2B-1440.weakness: The time range is smaller and lighter than “Wednesday”, although both are needed to identify the slot.
2B-1440.repair: Give “4–6 pm” at least the same size and weight as the weekday.
2B-1440.strength: Keyboard focus lands directly on the checked confirmation, making the outcome easy to find on a wide card.

primary_action.input: Press Tab to “Reserve shift”, then Space.
primary_action.expected: Show one Wednesday 4–6 pm Packing booking and move focus to its confirmation.
primary_action.observed: One booked Packing card appeared with the correct day and time. Focus outlined the full-width green “Shift booked” paragraph where the reserve button had been.

2B-390.edge_observation: One reload preserved exactly one booked Packing entry for Wednesday 4–6 pm. Its confirmation remained and focus returned to the document body.
2B-390.weakness: The full-width, outlined “Shift booked” paragraph has the shape and placement of another button.
2B-390.repair: Use a compact checked status beneath the time and move the visible focus outline to the booked card.
2B-390.strength: The confirmation occupies the same place as the action just taken, so the change is easy to spot on the phone.

1.reason: Both suggestions found the available saw at both widths. A put focus in the editable query, supplied a status naming the saw, and removed the match when the field was cleared. B kept the old result below an empty field.

2.reason: Both pages confirmed one booking and preserved it after reload at both widths. A gave the time more visual weight and focused the complete booking, keeping Packing, Wednesday 4–6 pm, and the confirmation together. B’s phone confirmation looked like a second action.
